text.p: Four Mexican businessmen suing Mexico's Grupo Financiero Abaco say the company owes $170 million from offshore invesments, newspaper Reforma said on Friday.

The newspaper cited attorneys in the suit against Abaco head Jorge Lankenau Rocha as saying the financial group carried out transactions with the company's capital. They said they did not expect Abaco to have the funds to cover its debt.
The suit will be for less than the total invested, the attorney's office said.

"Given that the trades were made by Abaco employees using company facilities, the financial group is responsible for the management and results of these investments," the attorney's office was quoted as saying.

It added that the company that acquires Abaco, currently up for sale, would be required to take up the lawsuit. Officials from Mexico's Securities and Banking Commission (CNBV) have said the group's buyer would not be responsible for the suit.
Abaco officials were not available for comment early on Friday.
Citicorp's Citibank is expected to win the bidding for the banking group, which needs a cash injection of about $250 million to comply with capitalization levels in the Mexican banking system.
